clue.text: Employ prison warders to intimidate

definitions.meaning: to put on staff is to employ them, and screws is slang for prison warders, so the phrase can be read literally
to bully or pressure someone into compliance

explanation.surface: A jail governor hires guards to frighten the inmates.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying screws to someone is an idiom for pressuring or coercing them; read literally it is taking on jail guards.

clue.text: Every year getting seaweed is a tedious business

parts.note: PA is per annum, Latin for each year
laver is an edible seaweed

explanation.surface: Collecting seaweed annually is described as a dreary chore.
explanation.definitionFit: A palaver is a fuss or a lengthy, tiresome procedure.

clue.text: Version containing new rite leads to an exchange of letters

indicators.note: the word for version holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a translation is a version of a text in another language

indicators.note: new suggests the word rite is remade in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A new ceremony included in a version of a text produces correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns RITE into ITER, and 'containing' puts it inside TRANSLATION after TRANSL.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing a word in another alphabet swaps each character for its counterpart in a different script.

clue.text: Conceal the coat

definitions.meaning: to keep something out of sight
an animal's skin or pelt

explanation.definitionFit: To cover something up is to keep it secret; an animal's pelt is its skin.

clue.text: Light American carriage found in Southern England

definitions.meaning: a four-wheeled two-seater horse-drawn vehicle
a home county just south of London

explanation.definitionFit: A surrey is a light four-wheeled buggy in the US; SURREY is also a county in southern England, south of London.

clue.text: About to pay up and move elsewhere

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
to settle a bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: Someone is about to clear their debts and relocate.
explanation.definitionFit: To relocate, especially to set up a new home in another place.

clue.text: Forever aimless

definitions.meaning: endlessly, eternally
lacking any goal, with end meaning purpose

explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal never stops; an end can also be a purpose, so lacking one is drifting.

clue.text: Her afternoon tea is served in quick succession

indicators.note: serving something up suggests the letters are dished out in a new order

explanation.surface: A lady's afternoon tea is brought out promptly.
explanation.definitionFit: Things happening consecutively follow each other in turn without a break.

clue.text: Minister provides a bit of fun in church

indicators.note: the bit of fun is placed within the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a lark is a prank or bit of fun

explanation.surface: A clergyman supplies some amusement during a service.
explanation.walkthrough: Minister suggests a cleric, but it is Kenneth Clarke, a British Cabinet minister and Chancellor.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenneth Clarke held several posts in British government, including Chancellor of the Exchequer.

clue.text: Hero-worshipper

parts.note: read as the lover of Hero, the priestess in Greek myth who was swum to across the Hellespont nightly

explanation.definitionFit: In legend this youth adored the priestess Hero and drowned crossing the Hellespont to reach her.

clue.text: Osbert and Sachaverell were artists' models

definitions.text: Osbert and Sachaverell were artists' models

parts.words: Osbert and Sachaverell were artists' models
parts.note: the literary brothers' surname split in two describes posing well for a painter

explanation.definitionFit: Osbert and Sacheverell were the literary brothers of that surname; good models pose skilfully for painters.

clue.text: Enormous tax round the south

indicators.note: the tax word goes round the letter for south

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A huge tax is levied around the south of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense, extremely large in size or extent.

clue.text: Produced footwear not without appeal-but overstepped the mark

indicators.note: produced suggests the letters are made into something new

parts.note: O is an appeal or invocation, as in O Lord

explanation.surface: Making shoes was unattractive, but someone pushed it too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes O out of FOOTWEARNOT before the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Going beyond acceptable limits is exceeding what is reasonable.

clue.text: Endure terrible danger in a riotous assembly

parts.note: to bear is to endure

indicators.note: terrible suggests the word danger is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone must put up with dreadful peril amid a rowdy crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear garden is a scene of noisy disorder, from the old bear-baiting arenas.

clue.text: Complained bitterly and made tracks

definitions.meaning: ranted or protested angrily
literally laid rails, as for a railway

explanation.definitionFit: To rant is to protest angrily; railway tracks are built from rails.

clue.text: No-one in this place is compos mentis

definitions.meaning: read as nobody missing from that spot, everyone present
Latin for of sound mind

explanation.definitionFit: Having full mental faculties is the idiom; literally everyone is present at that location.

clue.text: Be that as it may, a hairpiece needs support

parts.note: but means however, nevertheless
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Nevertheless, a wig requires something to hold it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttress is a structure built against a wall to prop it up.

clue.text: Get away with a clip around the ear

indicators.note: the word for a clip is placed round the ear

parts.note: a clout is a blow, a clip round the ear
taken as the word ear

explanation.surface: Someone escapes with only a smack on the side of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave quickly is to depart or scram.

clue.text: What it costs to produce electricity

definitions.meaning: a price or fee
an electric ... is a quantity of electricity

explanation.definitionFit: A fee is the price asked; a battery stores an amount of electrical energy.

clue.text: Mental patients may be treated there

definitions.meaning: relating to the mind, inner
read as in a hospital ward

explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts belong to the mind; hospital patients lie in a ward.

clue.text: Rats get their come-uppance

definitions.meaning: rats on, abandons
what one deserves

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rats abandons a cause; a just reward or punishment is what one deserves.

clue.text: Make hay now in whatever way you will

indicators.note: make suggests the letters are fashioned into a new word

explanation.surface: Farmers urged to make hay immediately, however they can.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in any manner at all, regardless of method.

clue.text: A woman holds an airtight container that is unbreakable

indicators.note: the woman word holds the container inside it

parts.note: a dame is a woman
a tin is a sealed container

explanation.surface: A lady keeps a sealed can that cannot be broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard as diamond; impossible to shatter.

clue.text: Mr Ackland's Chinese idol

definitions.meaning: ... Ackland was an English actor
a figure of a deity in Chinese worship

explanation.definitionFit: Joss Ackland was a British actor; a joss is a Chinese religious figure, as in joss stick.

clue.text: Keep on living the French way

parts.note: la is French for the
ST is street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone continues to live in the French manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure or survive is to go on existing.

clue.text: Good puzzle set by a scone producer

parts.note: a riddle is a puzzle

explanation.surface: A good puzzle is set by someone who bakes scones.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat iron plate on which drop scones are cooked.

clue.text: Warm woman in the shrubbery

parts.note: to heat is to warm
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A heated woman hides among the bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A low shrub of moorland, so a plant of the shrub kind.

clue.text: Single words expressing personal conditions

parts.note: alone, by oneself
terms are words or expressions

explanation.surface: Individual words are used to describe one's own circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: Conditions that suit oneself, set by the individual rather than others.
